title: Cell-type-specific eQTLs underlie the genetic architecture of complex traits.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded supplementary workbook MOESM3 (20.9 MB xlsx, no login needed) and parsed every sheet. Table S3 (OneK1K, cis-only): 10,288 genes (Ensembl IDs, unique, 0 missing values), 56 columns giving per-gene shared and cell-type-specific genetic variance for 7 cell types, plus SEs (standard errors), p-values, shared_h2, specific_h2 and specificity, with a column legend in the sheet header. Table S13 (CLUES/ImmVar replication cohorts): 10,553 genes, 40 columns. 9,888 genes appear in both. Agreement of per-gene specificity between the two cohorts: Spearman 0.063 (all genes), 0.146 (genes with total h2 > 0.05), 0.49 on the 179 genes nominally significant in both. OneK1K: only 800 genes have p:V (cell-type-specific genetic effect) < 0.05, against ~514 expected by chance out of 10,288; CLUES: only 99. 3,205 OneK1K genes have negative shared_h2 and 4,278 negative specific_h2 (estimates are unconstrained). Specificity ranges from -1,393 to 4,857. Also checked the CIGMA code repo (GitHub Minhui-Chen/CIGMA, GPL-3.0; Zenodo 19424343 is the software only) and the OneK1K site (original 2022 eQTL tables on S3, open).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (article paywalled, no PMCID, no full text in Europe PMC). The cohort sizes (928 individuals, 7 cell types, ~1,190 cells per individual) come from a search-result snippet of the article, not from the files. Other supplementary file numbers (MOESM1, 2, 4) returned 403 and were not inspected.

a1_downloadable.note: Per-gene result tables download openly as a 20.9 MB supplementary xlsx (verified). Underlying single-cell data and genotypes for OneK1K are listed publicly (GEO GSE196830, per OneK1K site) but were not needed or checked.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Yes: 'specificity', 'shared_h2' and 'specific_h2' are columns in Tables S3 and S13 (verified). Nothing has to be constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Only Ensembl gene IDs are present; gene features (constraint, enhancer counts, network degree, promoter sequence) would come from one standard-key join each, which is acceptable for ~10k genes.

a4_units_stated.note: Variance components and heritability fractions, defined in the sheet legend (verified); unitless and consistent.

a5_enough_rows.note: A5 in disguise: 10,288 rows, but the label is mostly noise. Only 800 genes have a nominally significant cell-type-specific genetic effect (about 514 expected by chance), and just 179 are significant in both cohorts. Cross-cohort per-gene agreement is Spearman 0.063 (computed from the files).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 10,288 genes and 7 cell-type columns in Table S3 match the 10,288 genes / 7 cell types quoted from the article snippet.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is a statistical variance-component (CIGMA) estimate fit to measured single-cell expression and genotypes, not another ML model's output and not computed from gene features. The problem is noise, not circularity.

existing_models.name: scooby (Nature Methods 2025), a Borzoi-based sequence-to-single-cell-expression model
existing_models.score_and_split: Used OneK1K fine-mapped cell-type-specific eQTLs to assess variant-effect prediction (from search snippet only; numbers not retrieved).

existing_models.name: CIGMA, this paper's variance-component model (statistical, not ML)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not a predictor; produces the per-gene estimates themselves.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Enformer/Borzoi cell-type tracks around each gene's promoter (DNA sequence models); none tested

integration.partner_dataset: gnomAD constraint (LOEUF), ABC enhancer–gene maps, GTEx
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which gene properties predict whether a gene's genetic regulation is cell-type-specific, the property the paper links to complex-trait heritability.

controls.positive_control: Paper's reported association of specificity with gene constraint (LOEUF) should be recovered.
controls.external_validation: Table S13 CLUES/ImmVar estimates for 10,553 genes, but these agree with OneK1K at Spearman 0.063.

honest_claim_h3: At best: gene-level features weakly rank the few hundred genes with detectable genetic effects by cell-type specificity in blood immune cells, in mostly European cohorts; per-gene labels are too noisy to support more.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene properties and DNA sequence to predict whether a gene's inherited expression differences show up in all immune cell types or only some.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per gene (10,288 genes verified) with gene-level features joined by Ensembl ID, such as mutation intolerance, enhancer count and network connections.
plain_idea.predict: The fraction of genetic expression variance that is cell-type-specific, estimated by the authors' variance-component model from single-cell RNA data on ~1,000 blood donors.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Geneticists prioritising disease genes could flag genes whose regulation is likely cell-type-specific without single-cell cohorts; but the label proves too noisy to learn from per gene.

label_elsewhere.sources: Original OneK1K per-cell-type eQTL tables (onek1k.org, verified listed); eQTL Catalogue single-cell datasets (known resource). Sharing could be computed from these, but that would mean constructing the label.
label_elsewhere.why: Other cohorts could give replicate estimates, but the one replication here (CLUES) already shows near-zero agreement.

ml_idea: Gene-level regression of cis-eQTL cell-type specificity (Table S3) on constraint, enhancer and network features plus sequence-model embeddings, validated on CLUES (Table S13). Killed by label noise: the two cohorts agree at Spearman 0.063 per gene.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from table size (10k rows); nothing timed beyond parsing the xlsx in seconds.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: cross-cohort Spearman of per-gene specificity = 0.063 (0.49 on only 179 genes significant in both), so the per-gene label has no usable signal.

verdict_reason: The labels are clean, open and in columns, but they are almost all noise. Per-gene cell-type specificity replicates between OneK1K and CLUES at Spearman 0.063. Only 800 of 10,288 genes have a nominally significant specific effect (about 514 expected by chance), and just 179 are significant in both cohorts. That is an A5 failure in disguise, and it leaves no learnable target.
